name: Rib cartilage rhinoplasty
lead: Rib cartilage rhinoplasty is nose surgery in which cartilage harvested from the patient's rib (costal cartilage) is used for structural grafts. General references note that septal cartilage is the preferred graft source and that rib or ear cartilage is used when septal cartilage is insufficient [1].

It is most associated with major dorsal reconstruction, revision cases and extended grafts such as the columellar strut. A retrospective cohort of 58 rib graft patients treated from 2000 to 2009 assessed graft stability, warping, need for revision and donor-site morbidity [2], and a later paper described anchoring an extended columellar strut with rib graft [3].
Published evidence is limited to a small number of surgeon case series.
infobox: Major dorsal augmentation, revision rhinoplasty, extended tip support
Septal or ear cartilage, allograft, synthetic implants

paras: Rhinoplasty references list septal cartilage as the first choice for grafts, with rib or ear cartilage used when septal cartilage is not enough, and bone or synthetic implants as further options [1]. Rib cartilage provides a larger quantity of material, which is why it is described for extensive reconstructions [2].

In the 58-patient retrospective study, investigators evaluated graft viability, mobility, warping, maintenance of dorsal projection, airway function, revision rates and donor-site problems through telephone follow-up; the authors described the technique as stable and predictable for major dorsal reconstruction [2].

Using rib adds a second surgical site. The 2011 study specifically assessed donor-site morbidity and graft warping as outcomes [2]. General rhinoplasty references report that revision surgery accounts for roughly 5 to 20 percent of operations [1].

Published human data consist of a retrospective cohort of 58 patients [2] and a technique paper on anchoring an extended columellar strut [3]. A registered study of allograft cartilage in cosmetic and reconstructive rhinoplasty (NCT05566808, 50 participants, completed) is listed, though it concerns a different graft source [4]. No randomized trials of rib cartilage were found.

timeline.event: Retrospective study of osseocartilaginous rib graft dorsal augmentation, 2000-2009 cases [2].
Technique described for anchoring an extended columellar strut in rib graft rhinoplasty [3].

card.summary: Nose surgery that uses rib cartilage for large structural grafts, mainly in major reconstruction and revisions; evidence is limited to small surgeon series.
card.note: Adds a chest donor site; evidence is mainly small case series.

quick.overview:
Rib cartilage rhinoplasty uses cartilage taken from the rib to build or rebuild the nose when septal or ear cartilage is not enough, such as in major dorsal reconstruction or revisions.

The published evidence is limited to a few surgeon case series.
quick.mechanism: Carved rib cartilage supplies firm structural grafts for the nasal bridge and tip support.
quick.risks: It adds a donor site on the chest, and studies track graft warping and donor-site problems. Rhinoplasty revision rates are roughly 5 to 20 percent overall. It is a surgical procedure.
